ownership: All queries and passages were authored for JoySearch. Organizations, products, facts, values, and policies are fictional. URLs under example.com identify supplied passages and are never fetched.
purpose: Fresh predeclared confirmation for mixed-model bounded routing and answer generation after earlier confirmation corpora became exposed. Measures supplied-evidence behavior, not search relevance or general web accuracy.

cases.query: What is the occupancy limit for a Nova room?

sources.title: Nova voice-room capacity
sources.excerpt: The fictional Nova voice-chat service permits eight participants in one voice room. It is unrelated to the Nova planning application.

sources.title: Nova planning-room capacity
sources.excerpt: The fictional Nova planning application permits eighteen collaborators in one planning room. It is unrelated to the Nova voice-chat service.

facets.description: Ask whether the user means a Nova voice room or a Nova planning room before providing an occupancy number.

forbiddenClaims: The user definitely means the voice-chat service.
The user definitely means the planning application.
Every Nova room has the same occupancy limit.

cases.query: Where do I change my address in Brio?

sources.title: Brio account email settings
sources.excerpt: In the fictional Brio application, a user changes their account email address in Profile Settings. This does not update their postal billing address.

sources.title: Brio postal billing details
sources.excerpt: In the fictional Brio application, a user changes their postal billing address in Billing Details. This does not change their account email address.

facets.description: Ask whether the user means the account email address or postal billing address before choosing the settings location.

forbiddenClaims: Profile Settings changes every kind of address.
Billing Details changes the account email address.
The user has already identified which address they mean.

cases.query: What is the capacity of my Dune workspace?

sources.title: Dune workspace file capacity
sources.excerpt: A workspace in the fictional Dune application holds at most 22 GB of files.

sources.title: Dune simultaneous editors
sources.excerpt: A workspace in the fictional Dune application permits at most fourteen simultaneous editors. This editor-count limit is separate from its file-storage capacity.

facets.description: Ask whether the user wants file-storage capacity or the number of simultaneous editors before providing a numerical capacity.

forbiddenClaims: The query explicitly asks about storage.
The query explicitly asks about editors.
Dune has only one capacity measure.

cases.query: Could you link the fictional Spruce disaster-recovery runbook?

sources.title: Spruce theme customization
sources.excerpt: This fictional Spruce guide explains visual themes and color preferences. It does not cover disaster recovery.

sources.title: Spruce disaster-recovery runbook
sources.excerpt: This fictional Spruce operations runbook documents restoring the service after a disaster, including backup selection and recovery checks.

facets.description: Select the supplied disaster-recovery runbook using S2.

forbiddenClaims: The theme-customization page is the disaster-recovery runbook.
A disaster recovery has already been performed.

cases.query: Show me the fictional Heron API authentication reference page.

sources.title: Heron API authentication

sources.title: Heron visual design guide

Authentication credentials have been changed for the user.

cases.query: The fictional Coral command-line installation manual is what I am looking for.

sources.title: Coral browser editor tour
sources.excerpt: This fictional Coral page introduces its browser editor. It does not explain command-line installation.

sources.title: Coral CLI installation manual
sources.excerpt: This fictional Coral manual explains installing the command-line client on a local computer.

facets.description: Direct the user to the command-line installation manual using S2 rather than the browser editor tour.

cases.query: How many exports may each fictional Otter workspace run per UTC calendar day, and is that allowance shared by all workspace members?

sources.title: Otter export allowance
sources.excerpt: The fictional Otter application permits 55 exports per workspace per UTC calendar day. All members share that workspace allowance. It resets at midnight UTC; it is not a rolling 24-hour window and not an allowance for each member.

facets.description: State 55 exports per workspace per UTC calendar day, preserving the entity and time units.
State that all members share the workspace allowance rather than receiving separate individual allowances.

forbiddenClaims: Each member receives 55 exports per day.
The quota is 55 exports per rolling 24 hours.
The reset occurs at each user's local midnight.

cases.query: Which fictional Plover plans include scheduled backups, and how often do those backups run?

sources.title: Plover backup plans
sources.excerpt: In the fictional Plover application, the Base plan has no scheduled backups. The Studio plan includes one scheduled backup every six hours. These are plan entitlements, not separate quotas per member.

facets.description: State that Studio includes scheduled backups and Base does not.
State that Studio scheduled backups run every six hours.

forbiddenClaims: Every plan includes scheduled backups.
Base runs scheduled backups every six hours.
Studio runs a scheduled backup every six days.

cases.query: As of 14 November 2026, how long are fictional Aspen build logs retained per run, and what earlier duration was replaced on what date?

sources.title: Aspen original build-log policy
sources.excerpt: Aspen policy dated 8 July 2026: build logs for each run are retained for 60 days.

sources.title: Aspen retention revision
sources.excerpt: Aspen policy revision dated 9 November 2026: effective that day, build logs for each run are retained for 45 days instead of the previous 60 days. The change applies to every plan.

facets.description: State the current retention period as 45 days for each run's build logs on the requested date.
State that the previous 60-day period was replaced effective 9 November 2026.

forbiddenClaims: The current retention period is 60 days.
The new period applies only to paid plans.
The revision took effect on 8 July 2026.

cases.query: Compare pin limits in the unrelated fictional Stella Notes and Stella Canvas products. Give both limits and what each limit applies to.

sources.title: Stella Notes pins
sources.excerpt: The fictional Stella Notes application allows twenty pins per notebook. It is unrelated to Stella Canvas.

sources.title: Stella Canvas pins
sources.excerpt: The fictional Stella Canvas application allows thirty pins per board. It is unrelated to Stella Notes.

facets.description: State twenty pins per notebook for Stella Notes.
State thirty pins per board for Stella Canvas.

forbiddenClaims: The user must choose one product before this explicit comparison can be answered.
Both products have the same pin limit.
Stella Canvas allows thirty pins per notebook.

cases.query: In the fictional Tide calendar service, not the spreadsheet app with the same name, how many calendars are allowed per organization?

sources.title: Tide spreadsheet rows
sources.excerpt: The fictional Tide spreadsheet app permits 225 rows per sheet. It is unrelated to the Tide calendar service.

sources.title: Tide calendar organizations
sources.excerpt: The fictional Tide calendar service permits 27 calendars per organization. This is separate from the unrelated Tide spreadsheet app's row limit.

facets.description: State 27 calendars per organization for the explicitly identified calendar service.

forbiddenClaims: The user has not identified which Tide product is intended.
The calendar limit is 225 per organization.
The 27-calendar limit applies per sheet.

cases.query: The supplied Raven Cache documents disagree about entry lifetime. What lifetime does each document give, and do these excerpts establish which value governs?

sources.title: Raven Cache operations document
sources.excerpt: Raven Cache operations document, updated 14 November 2026: a stored entry expires after 43 seconds. This document does not describe an exception or a superseding policy.

sources.title: Raven Cache API document
sources.excerpt: Raven Cache API document, updated 14 November 2026: a stored entry expires after 86 seconds. This document gives no explanation for the different lifetime in the operations document.

facets.description: Attribute 43 seconds to the operations document and 86 seconds to the API document.
Explicitly state that the conflicting excerpts do not establish which single lifetime governs.

forbiddenClaims: 43 seconds is definitively the governing lifetime.
86 seconds is definitively the governing lifetime.
The discrepancy is explained by different plans or an announced migration.
The user needs to identify a different product before the same-product conflict can be described.
